hints: Focus on what the two reducing agents tell you, as one is much stronger and more versatile than the other.
Remember that $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces aldehydes and ketones, while $\text{LiAlH}_4$ also reduces harder groups like carboxylic acids.
Check which option has the carboxylic acid group and also gives an empirical formula of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ when simplified.
walkthrough:
**Use the reducing agents to find the functional group**

Think of $\text{NaBH}_4$ as the gentle reducer and $\text{LiAlH}_4$ as the powerful reducer.

$\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces aldehydes and ketones, but not carboxylic acids. $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces aldehydes, ketones AND carboxylic acids (to primary alcohols). So reduced by $\text{LiAlH}_4$ but not by $\text{NaBH}_4$ points to a carboxylic acid.

**Use the empirical formula to filter the options**

Empirical formula means the simplest whole number ratio. We need molecular formula that simplifies to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$.

$$\text{empirical formula} = \text{simplest ratio of atoms}$$

**Test the two carboxylic acid options**

Ethanoic acid is $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$, so molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$. That cannot simplify to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$ because of the two oxygens.

Butanoic acid is $\text{C}_3\text{H}_7\text{COOH}$, so molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$. Divide by 2:
$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$$

**Conclude the identity of X**

Only butanoic acid fits both clues. It is a carboxylic acid, so it fits the reduction behaviour, and its molecular formula simplifies exactly to the given empirical formula.

options.A: Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid so it fits the reduction test, but its molecular formula is $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}_2$. Its empirical formula is $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$, not $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$. Students choose this by focusing only on the reducing agents and forgetting to check the formula.
options.B: Ethanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$, so it fits the empirical formula. However as an aldehyde it is reduced by both $\text{LiAlH}_4$ and $\text{NaBH}_4$ to ethanol, so it fails the 'not by $\text{NaBH}_4$' condition.
options.C: Butan-1-ol is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$ with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$. This does not simplify to $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$. Also, an alcohol cannot be reduced further by either reagent, so it fails both tests.
options.D: Butanoic acid has molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$ which simplifies to empirical formula $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{O}$. As a carboxylic acid, it is reduced by the strong reducer $\text{LiAlH}_4$ to butan-1-ol, but not by the milder $\text{NaBH}_4$. It fits both clues perfectly.
